record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.original_question: Let a polyomino be a strongly connected union of axis-aligned unit squares on the square lattice. Is there an algorithm that decides whether a given polyomino has any tiling of the plane at all, without restricting to isohedral tilings?

evidence.quote: Definitions. A polyomino is a subset of R2 formed by a strongly connected union of axis-aligned unit squares centered at locations on the square lattice Z2.
On the other extreme, it remains unknown whether there’s an algorithm for finding any tiling at all for a given polyomino.
Open Problem 4 Is determining whether a polyomino has a tiling decidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A polyomino is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ obtained as a strongly (edge-) connected union of finitely many axis-aligned closed unit squares whose centers lie at points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. A tiling of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by a polyomino $P$ is a covering of the plane by congruent copies of $P$ (allowing translations, rotations, and reflections) such that any two distinct copies have disjoint interiors. No restriction is placed on the symmetry type of the tiling (in particular, isohedral tilings are not assumed).

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input a polyomino $P$ (encoded, say, as a finite list of the integer coordinates of its constituent unit squares), decides whether $P$ admits at least one tiling of the plane?
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability of whether a single polyomino tiles the plane (allowing all rigid motions, no isohedral restriction) is widely cited as open. While the translation-only case for one polyomino is decidable (Beauquier–Nivat) and undecidability results have been established for sets of multiple polyominoes (e.g., 8 polyominoes by Ollinger; 5 polyominoes and 3 polygons in more recent work), the general one-polyomino case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Computational Complexity and Decidability of Tileability (Yang thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: The decidability of the k-polyomino tiling problem is open for small k; for a single polyomino with general isometries the question of decidability is unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The single-polyomino tileability problem (with general isometries) is recorded as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Undecidability of tiling the plane with a set of 5 polyominoes
status_evidence.snippet: Undecidability is established for sets of 5 polyominoes; the corresponding problem for a single polyomino remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Undecidability has been pushed down to k=5 polyominoes, while k=1 is still open.

status_evidence.title: Tiling the Plane with a Fixed Number of Polyominoes (Ollinger)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the hierarchy of k-polyomino tiling decidability problems with k=1 open.
status_evidence.claim: The 1-polyomino general tileability decidability is listed as open.
